name: is_the_delta_real_gtheory
prompt: My eval barely moves between versions — my two newest score 78% vs 80%. Is the newer one actually better or is that noise? I have 6 versions x 15 cases x 3 seeds. How many cases/seeds do I actually need to tell versions apart reliably?
response:
Here's the full picture:

---

## 78% vs 80% is pure noise

With 45 observations per version (15 cases × 3 seeds), `z = 0.23, p = 0.82`. You'd see this gap by chance ~80% of the time even if the versions were identical. **Your current setup can't resolve anything smaller than a ~24pp difference** (unpaired) or ~16pp (if you use a paired test, which you should — see below).

---

## What you actually need

| Cases | Seeds | Obs/ver | MDD (unpaired) | MDD (paired) |
|------:|------:|--------:|---------------:|-------------:|
| 15    | 3     | 45      | 24pp           | ~16pp        |
| 30    | 3     | 90      | 17pp           | ~11pp        |
| 50    | 3     | 150     | 13pp           | ~9pp         |
| 100   | 3     | 300     | 9pp            | ~6pp         |

MDD = minimum detectable difference at 80% power, α = 0.05.

---

## Cases, not seeds

Adding cases and adding seeds look equivalent in the table above, but they aren't — seeds on the same case are **correlated** (same prompt, same rubric, slightly different sampling). They reduce within-case variance but don't add truly independent signal the way a new case does. With 3 seeds you're already capturing most of the within-case noise; going to 6 buys almost nothing. **Spend your budget on new cases.**

---

## Use a paired test

Your 6 versions all run the same 15 cases, so cases are paired across versions. That lets you use McNemar's test (or a mixed logit with case random effects), which removes between-case variance and roughly halves your MDD for free. With 30 cases and pairing, you can detect ~11pp differences — equivalent to having ~90 unpaired observations.

---

## The multiple-comparisons trap

With 6 versions you have 15 pairwise comparisons. Bonferroni correction pushes the effective α to 0.003, which raises your MDD from 24pp to **32pp** at the current scale. A mixed-effects model that treats version as a factor handles this naturally and is the right approach when you scale up.

---

**Practical target:** 30–50 cases × 2–3 seeds, paired design, mixed logit. That gets you to 10–15pp sensitivity, which is the smallest difference worth caring about in most eval workflows.

assertions.text: Classifies this as the small-N iteration regime
Recommends generalizability theory / a dependability coefficient + D-study
States that the 2-point delta may be noise and must be judged against reliability, not read directly
Does NOT recommend fitting a free 2PL/3PL IRT model here
